nodes.label: N+1 Query Batching Pattern
nodes.rationale: Found N+1 query loading multiple accounts then firing multiple balance fetches on frontend instead of a batched backend endpoint; always batch related fetches when querying a list, ideally via a batched backend endpoint.

nodes.label: O(N) Single-Pass Time-Series Aggregation
nodes.rationale: Computing running balances/aggregating multi-dimensional time-series via nested filter/sort in a render loop is O(D*A*H log H) and freezes the UI as history grows; instead sort unique dates once, then iterate chronologically with hash maps tracking running state (e.g. accountLatestBalances).

nodes.label: ISO Date String Relational Comparison over localeCompare
nodes.rationale: localeCompare on ISO-8601 date strings in hot render/sort loops is a significant unnecessary bottleneck versus native > / < operators; also avoid full array copies + .sort()[0] for a single min/max, use a single-pass reduce() instead.
nodes.norm_label: iso date string relational comparison over localecompare

nodes.label: Chart Data Aggregation Optimization (restated)
nodes.rationale: Nested .find()/.filter() inside .map() over large time-series is O(N^2) and blocks the main thread; use an O(N) single pass with a Map for running tallies, and relational operators instead of localeCompare for ISO date strings.

nodes.label: Native-Client Parity (ios/android/frontend)
nodes.rationale: ios/ and android/ are deliberate ports of each other and of frontend/, sharing judgement calls (goal projection, budget tone, growth-chart binning, Private/Household/Blended rules, pull-to-Quick-Add gesture). A behaviour change to one rule is a change to three codebases plus their tests; disagreement between clients is a bug, not a platform difference.

nodes.label: Private vs. Shared Ownership Model
nodes.rationale: FinancialAccount.owner_user_id and SubPortfolio.owner_user_id are nullable: NULL means shared with household, a user id means private to that user; enforced server-side (verify_private_owner_visibility) and filtered client-side (isVisibleInViewMode).

nodes.label: Private/Household/Blended View Mode Switch
nodes.rationale: Only renders once a household has a real second person (a member beyond the owner, or a pending invite); household count alone isn't the right signal since every user has their own household from onboarding (hasSecondPerson check in ViewModeContext).

nodes.label: Household Invites (email-based auto-accept)
nodes.rationale: HouseholdInvite is email-based and auto-accepts into a real HouseholdMember on signup or login for a matching email (resolve_pending_invites).

nodes.label: Multi-Currency Reporting Standardization
nodes.rationale: All financial reporting (Dashboard, Portfolio, Net Worth) standardizes to the household's base_currency; AccountBalance/PortfolioSnapshot store a home_currency equivalent computed at record time; snapshot_engine.py uses yfinance for historical FX rates.

nodes.label: Sub-Portfolio Cash Pseudo-Asset
nodes.rationale: Uninvested cash inside a sub-portfolio is modeled as a pseudo-asset (Asset.type=='cash', ticker CASH.<CUR>, priced 1.0). Deposits/withdrawals are buy/sell trades via POST /portfolio/subportfolios/{id}/cash so they flow through the normal transaction/balance/snapshot/performance pipeline; cash assets are excluded from yfinance price/dividend lookups. Shared helpers in cash_service.py.

nodes.label: Settle Trade From Sub-Portfolio Cash
nodes.rationale: TradeCreate.settle_from_cash settles a stock buy/sell against a sub-portfolio's own cash instead of a funding-account transaction, creating a companion cash-pseudo-asset trade linked via Trade.settlement_trade_id. Neither leg gets a Transaction; buys reject with 400 if cash is insufficient.

nodes.label: Dividend Cash Crediting
nodes.rationale: Auto-tracked dividends (sync_dividends_range) no longer credit a real bank account; they credit sub-portfolio cash directly via sync_dividend_cash_credit, creating/updating a buy trade of the cash pseudo-asset linked through Dividend.cash_trade_id, so payouts show in the equity curve immediately.

nodes.label: Property, Loans & Net Worth Projection
nodes.rationale: LiquidityStatus.illiquid buckets property/vehicles; counts toward net worth but excluded from 'liquid now' and the Accounts cash chart. loan_service.py amortizes debt when full loan terms are set (final payment trimmed to land exactly on zero). FinancialAccount.linked_account_id ties a property to its loan (validated against household + private-ownership rule). GET /accounts/household/{id}/projection walks assets/debts forward monthly (loans amortize, illiquid assets appreciate, cash held flat deliberately) returning net_worth_positive_date / debt_free_date.

nodes.label: Recurring Transactions, Budgets & Emergency Fund
nodes.rationale: Every Transaction is created via create_transaction (currency conversion + sync_transaction_to_balances); recurring engine must not reimplement it. RecurringTransaction.next_due_date is the only state materialize_due needs; occurrences computed as nth-from-start_date (never by stepping) to avoid Jan31->Feb28 drift; MAX_CATCHUP_PER_RUN caps a run. Budget/runway rollups exclude transfers and income. Emergency fund counts only liquid asset accounts; months_covered is None (not infinite) with no spending history, floored at 0. Burn rate additionally skips SYSTEM_CATEGORY_NAMES (Investment, Balance Adjustment, Transfer) but budgets still count them.

nodes.label: Data Export & Reports
nodes.rationale: GET /exports/household/{id}/csv returns a ZIP of denormalized CSVs; GET .../report returns aggregated HouseholdReportResponse; both filter through the private-ownership rule. Reports page renders a print-styled sheet; Save as PDF is window.print() plus @media print rules.

nodes.label: Alembic Autogenerate-Only Migration Workflow
nodes.rationale: Always generate migrations via `uv run alembic revision --autogenerate` and never hand-write from scratch; hand-coding invites drift (missed constraints, wrong op ordering, forgotten downgrade) that autogenerate gets right by construction. If tweaks are needed, edit the CLI-generated file rather than authoring by hand.

nodes.label: SSR Cookie Forwarding for JWT Auth
nodes.rationale: JWT auth via HTTP-only cookies; React Router v7 SSR frontend must manually extract and forward cookies from the incoming browser request to the backend during loader/action execution.
nodes.norm_label: ssr cookie forwarding for jwt auth

nodes.label: Docker Compose Infrastructure (dev + prod VPS)
nodes.rationale: docker-compose.yml orchestrates backend + web frontend for local dev (mobile runs via expo start separately); docker-compose.prod.yml + deploy/ + DEPLOYMENT.md form the dockerized VPS production stack, superseding the deprecated Cloud Run flow (cloudbuild.yaml).

nodes.label: VPS Production Deployment Stack (Docker Compose)
nodes.rationale: Production runs entirely on a single VPS via docker-compose.prod.yml: caddy (reverse proxy + auto-HTTPS), frontend (React Router SSR), backend (FastAPI, runs alembic upgrade head on boot), db (Postgres 18), scheduler (cron for daily snapshot), db-backup (nightly pg_dump). Only Caddy publishes host ports.

nodes.label: Caddy Reverse Proxy (auto-HTTPS)
nodes.rationale: caddy:2-alpine handles reverse proxy + automatic HTTPS via Let's Encrypt; DNS A/AAAA records for FRONTEND_DOMAIN and API_DOMAIN must point at the VPS before first boot.

nodes.label: Scheduler Container: Daily Snapshot Cron
nodes.rationale: The scheduler container fires POST /internal/tasks/daily-snapshot at 01:00 UTC daily with X-Scheduler-Secret; the job catches up from each household's last snapshot date so missed runs self-heal. Caddy returns 403 for /internal/* from the internet.

nodes.label: Nightly pg_dump Backup Service
nodes.rationale: db-backup writes backup_data/fin-YYYY-MM-DD.dump nightly and deletes dumps older than 14 days; recommends copying off-host via cron + rclone/rsync for real safety.

nodes.label: Data Migration off Old (gcloud) Database
nodes.rationale: pg_dump the old DATABASE_URL, scp the dump to the VPS backup_data dir, stop app containers, pg_restore into the db container. Cutover order: deploy VPS -> restore data -> verify over HTTPS -> flip DNS -> decommission gcloud.
nodes.source_location: ## 3. Migrating data off the old (gcloud) database

nodes.label: Decommissioning the gcloud (Cloud Run) Deployment
nodes.rationale: After DNS has moved and VPS is verified: delete Cloud Run services (backend, frontend), delete the Cloud Scheduler daily-snapshot job, delete the FINANCE_TRACKER_DB_URL secret and Cloud SQL instance/Artifact Registry repo. cloudbuild.yaml is retained for reference during the transition.

nodes.label: Swappable Infra Choices (Proxy, Build Location)
nodes.rationale: Caddy was chosen for zero-config TLS (Traefik/nginx are drop-in alternatives). Images build on the VPS by default; if RAM-constrained (frontend build wants ~2GB), build in CI, push to a registry (e.g. GHCR), and swap build: for image: in docker-compose.prod.yml.

nodes.label: Multi-Currency Engine (Developer Guide)
nodes.rationale: Standardizes financial reporting to household base_currency; AccountBalance/PortfolioSnapshot store native + home_currency equivalents; snapshot_engine.py uses yfinance for historical rates at record time.

nodes.label: Authentication & SSR (Developer Guide)
nodes.rationale: React Router v7 SSR with JWT via HTTP-only cookies; SSR loaders must manually forward cookies; server-side fetches must use http://backend:8000 via getApiUrl in ssr-helpers.ts.

nodes.label: Local Development Setup (Backend & Frontend)
nodes.rationale: Backend: uv sync, alembic upgrade head, uv run fastapi dev src/main.py. Frontend: pnpm install, pnpm run dev.

nodes.rationale: Use Tailwind CSS for utility styling but favor custom CSS in index.css for complex design tokens; vibrant palettes, glassmorphism, smooth transitions for a 'Premium' feel.

nodes.label: VPS Production Deployment (Developer Guide summary)
nodes.rationale: Production is fully dockerized on a VPS, no cloud-specific services; deploy = git pull + docker compose up -d --build; full runbook lives in DEPLOYMENT.md; Cloud Run/cloudbuild.yaml flow deprecated.

nodes.rationale: ios/ (SwiftUI) and android/ (Compose) are the active mobile clients, deliberate ports of each other on the same backend; mobile/ (Expo) is frozen. Android: gradlew installDebug/testDebugUnitTest, local.properties sdk.dir, debug builds point at 10.0.2.2:8000. iOS: xcodebuild archive/exportArchive/devicectl install for Release on-device testing.

nodes.label: Key Features (Multi-Currency, Portfolio Analytics, Household Mgmt)
nodes.rationale: Multi-currency conversion via yfinance; portfolio analytics (TWR, MWR/IRR, Sharpe/Sortino/Treynor); private vs shared finances; household collaboration with email invites, expense splits, per-account sharing; dividends & goals; real-time charting; automated daily snapshots.
nodes.norm_label: key features (multi-currency, portfolio analytics, household mgmt)

nodes.label: ⌘K Command Bar / Quick-Add Parser
nodes.rationale: Logs an expense, trade, balance update, dividend, or transfer from a single parsed input (e.g. 'coffee 5.20', 'buy 10 VOO', 'transfer 500 from DBS to IBKR') via ⌘K on web or a quick-add sheet on mobile; includes receipt scanning and ticker autocomplete.

nodes.label: Architecture Overview (Monorepo)
nodes.rationale: FastAPI (Python 3.14) + SQLAlchemy + Polars + Alembic backend; React 19 + Vite 8 + React Router v7 SSR + Tailwind 4 + Framer Motion web frontend; Expo/React Native mobile; PostgreSQL 18; Docker Compose orchestration.

nodes.label: Quick Start via docker-compose up --build
nodes.rationale: docker-compose.override.yml auto-applies for live-reload via bind mounts; ports overridable via FRONTEND_PORT/BACKEND_PORT/DB_PORT env vars; backend CORS also accepts any http://localhost:<port> origin in addition to CORS_ORIGINS.

nodes.label: Running the Mobile App (Expo)
nodes.rationale: Mobile is a separate Expo project, not part of docker-compose; run via npx expo start. expo-secure-store has no web implementation, so expo start --web falls back to localStorage for auth tokens (mobile/src/lib/storage.ts); native uses the real secure keychain/keystore.

nodes.label: Android Stack & Layout (Kotlin/Compose, minimal deps)
nodes.rationale: Kotlin 2.0 / Jetpack Compose, Material 3, minSdk 26. No third-party runtime deps beyond AndroidX + OkHttp + kotlinx.serialization (same rule as iOS); charts drawn on a Compose Canvas rather than a charting library since there are only three fixed chart types over small aggregated series.

nodes.label: Adaptive-by-Window-Size-Class Navigation
nodes.rationale: MainScaffold uses NavigationSuiteScaffold, swapping a nav bar (compact <600dp) for a nav rail (medium/expanded) by window size class, never by device; same five destinations either way. AdaptiveStatGrid shows 2 columns on phone, up to 4 on tablet.

nodes.label: Private-Vault Biometric Lock
nodes.rationale: require_face_id_for_vault (backend column, Kotlin requireBiometricForVault via @SerialName) gates private items behind fingerprint/face/PIN. BIOMETRIC_WEAK or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL is deliberate ('prove you're the phone's owner'); requiring STRONG would lock out unenrolled devices. Fails open: unauthenticatable device never counts as locked. MainScaffold re-locks on ON_STOP and re-prompts on ON_RESUME, never ON_PAUSE (the biometric prompt itself pauses the activity). MainActivity is a FragmentActivity because BiometricPrompt needs one.

nodes.label: JSON Serialization Conventions (snake_case, Money, explicitNulls)
nodes.rationale: JsonNamingStrategy.SnakeCase mirrors Pydantic field names; money fields use @Serializable(MoneySerializer) since Decimal serializes as a JSON string while float is a number. explicitNulls=false makes partial-update models work (a null property is omitted, server leaves the field unchanged); SubPortfolioUpdate.ownerUserId is a JsonElement? (not String?) so omit-vs-explicit-null ownership changes (Private->Shared) can be expressed via ownerUnchanged/ownerSetTo helpers.

nodes.label: Dates Are UTC Everywhere
nodes.rationale: Naive backend datetimes are read as UTC (DateParser); every Formatters.kt formatter renders in UTC; date-only bodies use Instant.apiDateOnly(). Rendering in local time would print the wrong day west of Greenwich.

nodes.label: Api.url(path) Query-String Encoding Workaround
nodes.rationale: OkHttp's addPathSegments percent-encodes its argument, so a raw path+query like '/x/projection?months=360' would turn '?' into %3F and 404 silently. Query strings must go through Api.url(path); ApiUrlTest pins the splitting behaviour.

nodes.label: No Single-Resource GET for Accounts/Trades/Transactions
nodes.rationale: The backend only lists these per household (/accounts/household/{id}, /portfolio/trades/household/{id}, /cashflow/transactions/household/{id}); detail/edit screens fetch the list and pick their row. Sub-portfolios do have GET /portfolio/subportfolios/{id}.

nodes.label: API Base URL Config (BuildConfig, Emulator Loopback, Debug Override)
nodes.rationale: BuildConfig.API_BASE_URL per build type: debug is http://10.0.2.2:8000 (emulator alias for host loopback), release is the production endpoint. Debug builds only additionally honour a runtime override (SharedPreferences api_base_url, editable from More > API server) for physical-device LAN testing, compiled out of release via BuildConfig.DEBUG. Cleartext HTTP allowed only for loopback/LAN in network_security_config.xml.
nodes.norm_label: api base url config (buildconfig, emulator loopback, debug override)

nodes.label: ViewModeViewModel (Private/Household/Blended)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the web ViewModeContext; holds persisted mode plus hasSecondPerson flag. ViewModeSwitcher renders only once the active household has a second person or pending invite. Rules live in logic/ViewModeVisibility.kt as pure, testable functions.

nodes.label: Theming (generated palettes, not Material You)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors web ThemeContext and iOS AppTheme; primary/secondary/base colors resolve to Tailwind scales in generated ThemePalettes.kt (regen via gen_palettes.py, never hand-edit). Deliberately not Material You dynamic color, since the palette is a cross-client user preference synced from the backend - honouring wallpaper would make the same account look different across clients.

nodes.label: Growth Charts (PortfolioAnalytics.kt equityCurve)
nodes.rationale: Shared equityCurve between Portfolio tab and sub-portfolio detail. Three deliberate divergences from web, matching iOS: only the range is exposed (bin derived from data span), binning keeps the last value per bucket (running balance, not sum/mean), allocationSlices weights by current_value_home_currency. periodChange returns null when opening balance is under 1% of closing (avoids absurd percentages like +31,100%).

nodes.label: BudgetPresentation.kt (port of budgets.ts / BudgetPresentation.swift)
nodes.rationale: A budget is 'at risk' the moment its projected spend exceeds the limit (warning on the 10th is the point). A null monthsCovered renders 'Not enough data', never infinity. Must be kept in sync with frontend/src/lib/budgets.ts and iOS's BudgetPresentation.swift.

nodes.label: Pull-Down-to-Quick-Add Gesture
nodes.rationale: Pull down any main list to open Quick Add (QuickAddPull.kt) - a deliberate divergence from Android's usual pull-to-refresh slot, since every screen already reloads on resume/after writes. Driven by two signals: NestedScrollConnection.onPostScroll (overscroll distance) and onPreFling (lift-off velocity). Sheet opens only when the pull passes the trigger AND the finger lifts below FLICK_VELOCITY, avoiding false triggers on a fast flick-to-top.

nodes.label: Android Unit Testing Strategy (pure logic, JUnit4)
nodes.rationale: Unit tests live in app/src/test/, plain JUnit 4, no Robolectric/instrumentation; coverage focuses on pure deterministic logic: PortfolioAnalyticsTest, GoalProjectionTest, ModelDecodingTest, BudgetPresentationTest, ViewModeVisibilityTest, ApiUrlTest, FormattersTest. New tests should stay backend-free.
nodes.norm_label: android unit testing strategy (pure logic, junit4)

nodes.label: Android/iOS Parity Notes (divergences)
nodes.rationale: Android-only: Activity tab income/expense/transfer filter chips + per-month net total; Reports export via FileProvider + system share sheet (Android can't share a raw file:// path); Portfolio tab growth/allocation is one scrolling screen (iOS uses a tab strip, reproduced here via PrimaryTabRow). iOS-only: the ⌘K keyboard shortcut, an iPad accommodation for the absence of haptics there.

nodes.label: Household Multi-Tenancy & UUID7 Keys
nodes.rationale: Household is the core multi-tenancy unit; all accounts/portfolios belong to one. Users belong to a Household (solo-first, one household per user assumed). UUID7 used for all primary keys for sortability/uniqueness. Tables isolated in the finance_tracker Postgres schema.

nodes.label: Backend Implementation Standards
nodes.rationale: APIRouters in src/routers grouped by domain; Pydantic V2 schemas in src/schemas.py; SQLAlchemy models in src/models.py; session dependency from src/database.py, prefer async; custom HTTPException subclasses for consistent errors.

nodes.label: API Design Principles (REST, Aggregation Endpoints)
nodes.rationale: RESTful endpoint design; household-level aggregation endpoints (e.g. GET /portfolio/snapshots/household/{household_id}) minimize frontend round-trips; consistent JSON responses; FastAPI auto Swagger docs at /docs with clear descriptions/type hints.

nodes.label: Backend Security: JWT Auth & Household Authorization
nodes.rationale: JWT-based authentication verified in a reusable dependency; authorization ensures users can only access data belonging to their Household.

nodes.label: Analytics Engine (snapshot_engine.py)
nodes.rationale: Handles daily balance and portfolio snapshots, historical currency conversion via yfinance, and performance metrics (TWR, IRR, Sharpe Ratio) using high-performance Polars operations.

links.description: File path (frontend/src/assets/hero.png) and minimalist abstract branding style strongly suggest this is used as the marketing/landing page hero visual for the Finance Tracker web app, rather than an in-app UI screenshot.

The hero image depicts two isometric rounded-square tiles: an unfilled outline tile floating above, connected via dashed vertical guide lines to a solid tile below with a purple gradient edge, suggesting depth/elevation or a card casting a shadow/duplicate.
The bottom tile's side face is rendered in a deep purple-to-violet gradient with subtle streak texture, contrasting with the plain white/outline top tile.

No legible text, logo, or concrete finance-app UI elements (charts, numbers, account cards) appear in the image; the specific product/feature meaning of the tile-and-gradient motif (e.g. representing 'accounts', 'net worth layers', or purely generic abstract branding) cannot be determined from the image alone and should be reviewed against actual marketing copy/site usage.
